quotes.text: Most organizations invest 90% of their effort in visual customization and 10% in logical orchestration. The successful ones flip that ratio. They spend more time designing the flow of the event than decorating the space
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Latency is the real time performance that makes presence possible. Logic is the orchestration that makes presence meaningful. When latency fails, the space feels broken. When logic fails, the space feels empty.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: Microsoft Mesh now lives inside Teams as immersive spaces and events, so it inherits Teams licensing, identity, compliance and network paths, along with their limitations such as no web, mobile, VDI, Teams Rooms or dial-in support.
Treat immersive events as systems engineering: audit network paths, split tunneling and QoS, test hardware and Quest sign-in under conditional access, and keep a standard Teams meeting as a fallback.
Spend more effort on logic than on decoration, using server-mediated, collaborative activities, a 60-minute agenda and Power Platform-based registration and measurement.
hook: Immersive team events in Microsoft Teams often fail not because of the 3D technology but because of network latency, unequal hardware and missing orchestration. This episode shows Microsoft 365 admins and event organizers how to engineer latency and logic together, from network and Quest security checks to agenda design and Power BI measurement.
